en.question: A classification prompt performs well overall but consistently mislabels one rare category. What is the most targeted fix?

options.text: Move the workload to a larger model tier with stronger reasoning ability.
options.note: An expensive blunt instrument that may not resolve a definitional ambiguity.

options.text: Define that category precisely and show examples, including near-miss cases.
Increase max_tokens so the model has room to deliberate before labelling.
options.note: Output length is irrelevant to which label is chosen.

options.text: Drop the neighbouring categories so the rare one is no longer confusable.
options.note: Removing categories changes the task rather than solving it.

en.explanation: A single confused category is a boundary problem, so sharpen the boundary. Demonstrating true positives alongside the near-misses it is being confused with is targeted, cheap, and measurable.
